title: [FancyZones CLI] Help examples use a payload name that is not exposed on PATH
summary: FancyZones help advertises the internal payload name, not the public CLI shim that the installer puts on PATH.
next_action: Verify the command-name mismatch in an installed build and update root help, subcommand help, and examples to use the public shim.

judgment.rationale: The source confirms the naming mismatch, and the reporter observed it on extracted stable and preview installers. Installed-product PATH behavior still needs verification.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the installed public command and keep the internal payload directory off PATH.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix surfaced. The mismatch is in the help text rather than in command dispatch.

proposed_fixes.title: Use the public FancyZones CLI name in help and examples
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FancyZonesCliUsage prints FancyZonesCLI, while the installer exposes PowerToys.FancyZones.CLI.exe via its bin directory.
plan: Use the installed public executable name consistently in root and subcommand usage and examples.
Leave the shim mapping and installer PATH behavior unchanged.
Add coverage that checks displayed usage and examples reference the public shim.
verification: From a fresh terminal outside the install directory, copy a help example and verify that it reaches FancyZones after both per-user and machine installs.

confidence.rationale: The source and extracted installers agree; real installation and PATH propagation have not been independently verified.

actions.label: Verify the FancyZones help commands in an installed build

reproduce.title: Compare advertised FancyZones command names with installed command lookup
reproduce.version_requirement: Stable 0.102.3101.0 or preview 0.103.3151.0 plus a candidate build
prerequisites: Disposable Windows environment for per-user and machine installations.
setup: Enable the installer CLI PATH option, then start a fresh terminal in an unrelated directory; do not edit global PATH for the test.
steps: Check command lookup for PowerToys.FancyZones.CLI.exe and FancyZonesCLI.exe.
Run the public shim with --help and inspect usage and examples for the root and a subcommand.
On the candidate build, copy the displayed get-monitors example into the same terminal and check that it invokes FancyZones.
reproduce.expected_result: The baseline help advertises the internal name; the candidate uses the public shim in help and examples without adding the installation root to PATH.

actions.label: Align FancyZones help with the installed command name

issue_context.summary: FancyZones CLI help describes a command name not exposed by the installer.
known_information: The reporter confirmed the mismatch in extracted signed stable and preview payloads; this was not installed-product validation.
inferences: Changing the help text should address the mismatch without changing what the shim launches.
issue_context.analysis: The CLI shim manifest maps the public executable to the internal payload. This differs from #52186, where the reporter reached the CLI using the correct shim and received a missing-layout-file error.
initial_investigation: Root and subcommand examples use the internal executable name in FancyZonesCliUsage.cs: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/084281ef6b137aa47a1e6a8e1e7bf79b0fe0378e/src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesCLI/CommandLine/FancyZonesCliUsage.cs
The public entry point and relative target are defined in the shim manifest: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/084281ef6b137aa47a1e6a8e1e7bf79b0fe0378e/tools/CliShim/CliShimManifest.props
information_gaps: Confirm installed PATH behavior separately for per-user and machine installations.

status.label: Needs Repro
status.detail: Help-name mismatch confirmed in source; installed-product verification remains.
